_comment: The Liscor sewers canonical walkthrough. Loads the near_sewers FIXTURE (post_tutorial_street shape + heard_about_cisterns pre-banked, so the grate-gate is open -- the cisterns quest banks that accomplishment from Olesm for real) via title Continue, positioned two steps north of the grate approach. Enters via the REAL sewer_grate interact (door_when seam), walks the sewers, reads two flavor props, clears the sewer_vermin trash pack (autoplay), then climbs the exit ladder back to the street. Proves: the grate-gate transition, the sewers dark mood + map render + always-on ambience, prop toasts, the new sewer_vermin encounter/arena, and the exit door. Fixture rng_state (9) governs -- no --seed search. NOTE: the shield_spider nest is placed but NOT fought here (that is the cisterns quest's job; interact-only, off this path). PLAYTEST FEATURE 3 EXTENSION: after landing, casts [Light] on the ambient path (hotbar_2) to conjure the PC-following arcane glow that makes the dark sewers navigable -- proving the new light_active sim flag, the ui_pc_light_rendered{active:true} UI confirmation, the follows-you toast copy, and a LIT vs UNLIT screenshot pair (00_sewers_landing = unlit, 00b_sewers_lit = lit). The near_sewers fixture was given `light` in player_skills for this (see its comment); the cast is exploration-only and fight-determinism-neutral, so the vermin autoplay is unchanged.

steps._comment: == BURNABLE-PROP SEAM. The near_sewers PC knows [Firefly] (fire field skill, slot 4). Rotten debris (sewer_debris, burnable) blocks the dead-end nook at (1,2), one cell WEST of the landing. Face it and burn it -> the prop is removed PERMANENTLY (removed_entities, saved) and the nook opens. Nothing else treads x0-1, so this seam is invisible to every other sewers script. DISCLOSURE: this run now banks burned_the_debris:1 + marks [Firefly] used; no script asserts an exact accomplishments/used_skills dict. ==
The debris blocks (1,2), so the leftward step is refused -- PC stays at (2,2) now FACING the debris.

steps._comment: Walkability flip: the vacated cell is now open, so the same leftward step succeeds -> (1,2). The burn poof (hit_sparks reuse) fired at this cell; screenshot the cleared nook.
Back to the landing to run the freeze crossing.

== FREEZABLE-WATER SEAM. The PC knows [Snap Freeze] (slot 3). Channel-A cell (3,5) is a freezable crossing. Walk to (3,4) on the top band, face down at the water, prove it BLOCKS, frost-cast it into walkable ice, then step across -- the walkability flip. Ice thaws at the next sleep (not exercised here; the exit ladder ends the run). ==
The channel water at (3,5) blocks the downward step -- PC stays at (3,4) FACING it.

payload_contains.text: [Snap Freeze] — You lay your palm to the water and cold spiders out from it. In a breath the channel locks to grey-white ice, thick enough to bear your weight. It will not last past your next rest.

steps._comment: v0.15 A3 (GH#304): THE LOSSLESS-DELIVERY CHECKPOINT for the two [Skill] payoff narrations. Both were emitted (sim `toast`, pinned at their cast sites above) long before the fight; by the time the combat board has CLOSED, both must have RENDERED. That is the whole GH#304 regression: at 23aca0b 4 of this run's 7 pre-combat toast payloads were NEVER delivered (these two, the moss observe, and the autosave) vs 0 lost after. PACING-INDEPENDENT BY CONSTRUCTION (QA/SEWERS-WINDOWED-TIMING, and the CI red on PR #310): WHICH side of combat_started they render on is pure frame pacing, not behavior. Toast holds are wall-clock (QA_TOAST_HOLD_HEADLESS_SECONDS 0.05s), so the faster the frames, the LESS wall time the driver's moves burn and the more of the queue is still pending when combat_started banks it. On this laptop's headless frames 3 render pre-combat and 4 bank and drain after ui_combat_hidden (the restore's own kick); on CI's loaded runners -- and windowed at real-time frames -- the queue drains naturally pre-combat and nothing is left to bank. Both are correct engine behavior; only a cursor-ordered wait could tell them apart, and it red-flags the healthy half. So these are `from_start` scans (whole log, cursor untouched) placed AFTER the board closes: they hold in every pacing regime and still fail flat in the 23aca0b world where the payloads never render at all. The bank/restore branch itself -- `_restore_banked_toasts` kicking a drain when `_toast_draining` is false -- is pinned deterministically in tests/test_message_layer.gd, which is where a frame-rate-free proof belongs.

payload_contains.text: [Firefly] — The tarred rope takes the flame first and the pile goes after it. The nook stands open behind the ash, with the handle of an iron strongbox showing at the back of it.
[Snap Freeze] — You lay your palm to the water and cold spiders out from it. In a breath the channel locks to grey-white ice, thick enough to bear your weight. It will not last past your next rest.
